title: Greater domestic variability is caused by changed, less uniform conditions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Greater domestic variability is caused by changed, less uniform conditions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The greater variability of domestic productions is due to their being raised under conditions of life less uniform than, and somewhat different from, those of their parent species in nature.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I think we are driven to conclude that this greater variability is simply due to our domestic productions having been raised under conditions of life not so uniform as, and somewhat different from, those to which the parent-species have been exposed under nature.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter I, “Variation under Domestication”; section “Causes of Variability”. Scope: domesticated animals and cultivated plants

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch01-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Variables can be approximated, but historical exposure and causal attribution are weakly recorded. Existing crop and climate data permit only restricted, confounded tests.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across matched domestic lineages, regress heritable variation on quantified environmental heterogeneity and difference from ancestral habitat while controlling population size, admixture and selection. A positive independent effect supports the mechanism; its absence or dominance by breeding history refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ancestral husbandry environments are poorly documented.

Artificial selection and admixture confound environmental effects.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.32

analysis feasibility: 0.52
discriminating power: 0.36

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The causal contrast is definable, but the datasets that are easy to download record where cultivated plants differ, not whether uneven conditions produced that variability. A honest test needs common-garden or mutation-accumulation designs that are not assembled in one open archive. Existing compilations can describe domestic versus wild dispersion and leave the mechanism entangled with selection and crossing.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Hold ancestry constant and compare phenotypic or mutational variance of lines reared in uniform ancestral environments versus novel, less uniform ones, alongside a selection-relaxed control. A causal role for conditions would be supported if environmental novelty raised heritable variance when selection and hybridization were matched; no increase, or an increase explained by relaxed selection alone, would count against the stated cause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The relevant experiments exist as scattered supplements and cover few domesticated species.

Relaxed selection, hybridization, and larger census sizes are confounded with the change in conditions under domestication.

Public trait databases mostly store species means, not variances from common-garden designs.
